chapter_title: Concerning the Seed Grain that shall be formed by
spiritual_reading:
A living truth in potency, and the understanding of good that attends it, are brought into determinate form and ordered for use through a sufficient complement of fundamental states in the outer degree. Alternations of affection and obscurity sustain that truth in potency, and sustain the whole formed perception that grows from it. Yet as those alternations can sustain, so they can also fail; and when sustaining influx is withdrawn, the capacity to receive is laid waste by deprivation and the lack of appropriation.

So also, through such disordered states, deficiencies and lapses arise in successive particulars of life. Those who have chosen that disorder gather such deficiency into themselves, confirm it, and bring it to an apparent perfection, until distress and torment rise up within it from the very things by which it was fixed.

Through this, many are made to fall away, because the lower self that loves what is merely its own dwells within them and drives them. That self casts obscurity over their understanding; and in the same way it casts obscurity over fundamental truths in the outer mind, so that the works that should proceed from sound perception are ruined in their entirety.

fills.notes: The sequence “formed … and beautified by the five elements” requires an intermediate act of collecting and arranging prior to adornment. In the substrate register, the elements first receive, collect, and compact what is potential (seed) into a stable outer form before it is ‘beautified’ (perfected in its own degree).

fills.fill: and increase, and just as they strengthen it
fills.notes: Warmth and cold here are the alternating states that both nourish and (by right order) cause growth. The parallelism demands a second clause matching “nourish” with a further effect (“increase” or “strengthen”), preparing for the reversal in the next lacunae (what can nourish can also ruin).

The spiritual sense requires the failure-mode of alternations: when sustaining influx is absent, what was being nourished collapses. In the oldest layer this is expressed as the elements or their qualities ‘withdrawing’ rather than as moral fault.

The destruction is explicitly said to be “through … hunger.” In the substrate register, the corresponding natural cause is deprivation of sustaining supply: ‘lack of nourishment’ is the direct, impersonal complement to “hunger,” keeping the cosmological-causal tone rather than exhortative language.

assessment: All four gaps are recoverable at the level of correspondential structure: (1) an arranging or gathering act must precede ‘beautifying’; (2) nourishment must be paired with growth-strengthening before the reversal; (3) the reversal is best expressed as withdrawal of sustaining qualities; (4) the causal phrase must name deprivation of nourishment as the ground of ‘hunger.’ Exact Coptic equivalents could vary, but the demanded cosmological logic is tight.
